stem: Which quotation from a work by an art historian would most effectively illustrate the claim?
stimulus: In the 1950s, printmaker Teodora Lisn produced several hundred prints in a small studio in Lisbon. Early reviewers called her a woodcut artist, since many of her best-known works began as carved wooden blocks. Art historian Paulo Reis disagrees with that label. He argues that Lisn's distinctive style came from combining woodcut, etching, and lithography within single works.
choices: "Lisn carved her blocks from pear wood, which let her cut lines finer than most woodcut artists of her day could manage."
"In many of Lisn's sheets, a woodblock sets the broad shapes, an etched plate adds fine lines, and a lithographic stone adds gray tones."
"Lisn's prints are remarkable for their bold colors, which still look vivid after seventy years of exposure to gallery lighting."
"Lisn kept her printmaking methods strictly separate, believing that each technique should be shown in its purest form."
explanation: Reis's claim is not just that Lisn's prints were distinctive. It is that she combined three methods (woodcut, etching, and lithography) in a single work. Choice B shows all three working together on one sheet, so it matches the claim exactly.

A.why: You picked a quotation about the right artist and a real technique, but it covers only woodcut. A single tradition is exactly the label Reis is arguing against. Nothing here shows several methods being combined.

C.why: You chose a quotation that praises Lisn's prints. Durable color says nothing about mixing woodcut, etching, and lithography, so it is on topic but does not support the claim.

D.why: This quotation says Lisn kept her techniques apart, which is the opposite of combining them. It would weaken Reis's claim, not illustrate it.

stem: Which quotation from an excavation report would most effectively support the claim?
stimulus: Kerevan, a Bronze Age village in a river valley far from the sea, was long thought to have been largely self-sufficient. Its residents farmed barley, kept goats, and made their own pottery from local clay. Recent digs, however, have prompted archaeologist Hana Dursun to reconsider. Dursun claims that Kerevan's residents traded regularly with communities on the coast.
choices: "Pottery found at Kerevan closely resembles pottery from several other inland villages located farther up the same river valley."
"Kerevan's houses were built of mud brick on stone foundations, and most had a single hearth near the center of the main room."
"Marine shells, which could only have come from the coast over 200 kilometers away, turned up in nearly every Kerevan household."
"Every object recovered at Kerevan was made from materials that could be gathered within a day's walk of the village itself."
explanation: The claim links two specific groups: Kerevan's residents and coastal communities. Sea shells that could only have come from the coast, found in almost every household, show regular contact with the coast. That is the relationship the claim describes.

A.why: This quotation does show a connection, but it is between Kerevan and other inland villages. The claim is about trade with the coast, so this supports a link with the wrong group.

B.why: You chose an accurate-sounding detail about Kerevan, but house construction tells you nothing about trade with anyone.

D.why: If everything came from within a day's walk, Kerevan really was self-sufficient. This quotation supports the old view that Dursun is challenging, not her claim.

stem: Which quotation from the ecologists' field report would most effectively support the claim?
stimulus: Beavers build dams that slow streams and create quiet ponds. To learn whether these ponds help frogs, a team of ecologists surveyed twenty-four streams in a mountain forest. Twelve had active beaver dams, and twelve did not. Otherwise the two groups were matched for size, elevation, and surrounding vegetation. Team leader Marcus Oyelaran concluded that frogs breed more in dammed streams than in similar streams without dams.
choices: "The dammed streams held many frog egg masses, and several of the largest clusters were found within a few meters of a dam."
"The dammed streams held about three times as many frog egg masses as the undammed streams of matching size and elevation did."
"Beavers at the dammed streams felled dozens of young aspen trees, opening gaps in the forest canopy along the banks."
"Frog egg mass counts in the dammed streams were nearly identical to the counts recorded in the undammed streams."
explanation: Oyelaran's conclusion is a comparison: more breeding in dammed streams than in similar undammed ones. Choice B gives that comparison directly. Matched streams with dams had about three times as many egg masses.

A.why: This quotation reports lots of eggs in dammed streams, but it never compares them with the undammed streams. The claim is about the difference between the two groups, and this choice describes only one of them.

C.why: You picked a detail about what beavers do to the forest. Tree felling says nothing about how much frogs breed, so it does not support the claim.

D.why: Nearly identical counts would mean the dams made no difference. That undercuts the conclusion instead of supporting it.

stem: Which quotation from a work by a music critic would most effectively illustrate the claim?
stimulus: Composer Amalia Ostrova grew up in the mountain village of Brezna before training at a conservatory in Vienna. Her four string quartets, written in the 1920s, were admired in concert halls across Europe. Some critics treated them as purely academic works. Musicologist Irena Holub disagrees, claiming that Ostrova built her quartets on folk songs she had heard as a child in Brezna.
choices: "Ostrova's quartets drew steady praise from critics, who admired their emotional depth and their lively, unpredictable rhythms."
"In Vienna, Ostrova mastered the strict counterpoint of the German composers, and her quartets display that training throughout."
"Several melodies in Ostrova's quartets match, nearly note for note, songs that folklorists later recorded from singers in Brezna."
"None of Ostrova's quartet melodies resembles any of the folk songs that were collected in the region where she grew up."
explanation: Holub's claim ties the quartets to one particular source: folk songs from Brezna. Choice C shows quartet melodies matching songs recorded in Brezna almost note for note, which is direct evidence of that link.

A.why: You chose praise for the quartets. Admiring their depth and rhythm does not show where the melodies came from, so the quotation is on topic but does not support the claim.

B.why: This quotation does connect the quartets to a musical tradition, but it is the wrong one: Viennese conservatory training, not Brezna folk song. If anything, it backs the "academic" reading Holub rejects.

D.why: This quotation denies any resemblance to local folk songs, which is the opposite of Holub's claim.

stem: Which quotation from a study by geologists would most effectively support the claim?
stimulus: For decades, the Arlen Basin recorded only a few small earthquakes each year. After 2015, that number rose sharply. During the same period, energy companies began pumping large volumes of wastewater deep underground through wells scattered across the basin. Injected fluid can raise pressure along buried faults, making them more likely to slip. Seismologist Ruth Caldera argues that the wastewater injection caused the basin's increase in earthquakes.
choices: "Since 2015, most of the basin's earthquakes have been small, and only a handful have exceeded magnitude 3.0 on the standard scale."
"Nearly all of the basin's new earthquakes occurred within ten kilometers of an active injection well, and very few occurred elsewhere."
"Seismometers installed across the basin in 2014 can detect earthquakes far too faint for residents to feel at the surface."
"The rise in the basin's earthquakes began several years before the first wastewater injection well was drilled there."
explanation: Caldera's claim connects two things: injection wells and the new earthquakes. Choice B shows that the new quakes cluster near active wells and are rare elsewhere. That ties the quakes to injection, which is the link the claim needs.

A.why: You picked a quotation that describes the earthquakes, which is the right subject. It says nothing about wells or wastewater, though, so it cannot show that injection caused them.

C.why: This is a detail about the monitoring equipment. Knowing how sensitive the seismometers are does not connect the earthquakes to wastewater injection.

D.why: If the quakes increased before any well existed, injection could not have started the rise. This quotation weakens Caldera's claim.
